subject: RFI: audit evidence packaging, integrity manifests, and S3 delivery options
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice@greenco.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: security-team@greenco.com
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: evidence packaging and exportability details

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this question — our procurement/security team is collecting implementation-level details for the RFP. We need to understand exactly how Redwood packages and delivers audit/evidence artifacts for legal/forensic review. Specifically:

- What is the canonical export format(s) you support for audit trails (schema, sample record)? CSV/JSON/Parquet? NDJSON?
- Are timestamps normalized to UTC and do records include both event and ingestion timestamps?
- How do you guarantee integrity (hash manifests, signing, KMS-backed signatures)?
- Do you include monotonic sequence IDs or append-only offsets to prove ordering?
- What retention windows are configurable on hosted vs dedicated vs private? Can we request discrete exports for legal hold beyond retention windows?
- Export delivery options: S3 presigned upload, direct push to customer bucket, HTTPS transfer? Any support for mutual TLS or signed SFTP?
- Turnaround SLA for producing an evidence bundle and the typical size/throughput limitations.

Can you also provide a sample manifest and an overview of the package layout (index, schema, binary attachments, redaction notes)? We will attach the answers to the RFP record; simple, concrete examples are most helpful.

Appreciate quick confirmation.

Thanks,
Alice Monroe
Lead Security Analyst, GreenCo Solutions

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice@greenco.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, david_kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: evidence packaging and exportability details

Alice —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, implementation-oriented response you can paste into the RFP. I’ve attached a reference manifest and the export schema doc for clarity (see attachments).

1) Supported export formats and structure
- Primary formats: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) for event streams; Parquet for columnar analytics exports; optional gzip compression.
- Package layout: root manifest.json (SHA256-signed), /events/yyyy-mm-dd/*.ndjson, /indices/*.parquet, /attachments/<binary blobs>.bin, /redaction-notes.txt
- Each NDJSON record contains: event_id, sequence_id (monotonic per-tenant), model_version, event_timestamp (ISO8601 UTC), ingestion_timestamp (ISO8601 UTC), actor_id, route_id, request_token, payload_summary (redacted), retention_flag. See export-schema-v2.md for full field list.

2) Timestamps and ordering
- All timestamps are normalized to UTC (ISO8601) and we include both event and ingestion timestamps for forensic correlation.
- A monotonic sequence_id is assigned at write-time to preserve ordering across retries; sequence spans are contiguous within a retention shard and exported with start/end sequence markers in the manifest.

3) Integrity and tamper evidence
- Manifest (manifest.json) contains per-file SHA256 checksums and a top-level bundle signature. For Hosted customers we provide a server-side signature; for Dedicated/Private deployments we can sign manifests using customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) by request.
- We additionally produce a chain-of-custody log file listing export job id, operator, start/end times, and transfer checksum verification results.

4) Retention windows and legal hold exports
- Hosted: default audit log retention is 90 days. Hosted customers may purchase extended retention up to 2 years (product add-on).
- Dedicated: configurable retention policies up to 7 years via reserved capacity contracts.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): fully configurable by customer policy; retention and purge are under customer control.
- For legal hold: we support ad-hoc evidence exports that snapshot data outside the normal retention flow. We can produce preserved bundles and mark affected sequences as held to prevent garbage collection.

5) Export delivery and transfer options
- Delivery options: (a) Pre-signed S3 PUT to a customer-owned bucket, (b) Server-initiated PUT to customer S3 where credentials are provided via secure role assumption, (c) HTTPS POST to a customer endpoint, (d) SFTP (host-key verified) — mutual TLS available for HTTPS deliveries.
- All transfers include end-to-end checksum verification and are logged in the chain-of-custody.

6) SLA and throughput
- Typical hosted evidence bundle (30 days of audit events for a medium-size tenant) produces a ~1–5GB package and delivery completes in 1–3 business days.
- For large or longer-range exports we provide estimated delivery windows during intake; Dedicated customers can request prioritized/export-acceleration for an SLA (commonly 24–48 hours) as part of a contract.

7) Attachments and redaction
- Attachments (binary blobs) are packaged alongside event indexes. We include a redaction-notes.txt describing any redactions and the policy applied.

8) Forensic runbook and evidentiary artifacts
- We maintain a documented runbook (forensic-export-runbook.pdf) that describes verification steps auditors should perform. For litigation holds we can provide a notarized manifest (third-party timestamping) as an add-on.

Attachments included: redwood_audit_evidence_sample_manifest.json (example manifest), export-schema-v2.md (field-level schema), s3-delivery-instructions.pdf (transfer checklist).

Next steps: if this level of detail works, we can schedule a 30-minute technical intake to walk through a sample export (I recommend laura and david attend to cover NFRs and transfer ops). Proposed slots: Tue 6/1 10am PT or Wed 6/2 2pm PT.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Monroe <alice@greenco.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: security-team@greenco.com
Date: 2027-05-31T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: evidence packaging and exportability details

Jonas —

Thanks, that’s very helpful. A few clarifying items so we can finalize the RFP response:

- For the hosted 90-day retention option, is there a documented policy for soft vs hard delete? If a record is purged after retention, can you provide a preservation copy if legal hold is initiated retroactively?
- When you say "manifest signature" can you confirm the algorithm (SHA256 + RSA-2048 or ECDSA)? Who is the signer for hosted bundles?
- Do exported Parquet files include the same sequence_id and event_timestamp fields (i.e., schema parity)?
- For the S3 presigned PUT method, we will need the precise permissions and bucket policy example so our infra team can create the role.
- Cost: is there a standard example cost for a 30-day export bundle for a mid-size tenant (for SOW planning)?

If you can drop answers to those inline items we’ll include them. We’re also leaning toward the Tue 6/1 10am PT slot.

Best,
Alice

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice@greenco.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, david_kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: evidence packaging and exportability details

Alice — quick follow-up answers inline: 

- Soft vs hard delete: Hosted uses soft-delete tombstones for 30 days after which data is eligible for hard purge. We cannot retroactively recover hard-purged records for Hosted unless extended retention was purchased or a preserved snapshot was taken prior to purge. For legal holds, we snapshot and mark sequences as preserved to prevent GC.

- Manifest signature: default algorithm is SHA256 for checksums; signatures use RSA-2048 with PKCS#1 v1.5 by default for hosted bundles. For dedicated/private customers we support ECDSA (P-256) and customer KMS-backed signatures (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or on-prem HSM).

- Parquet parity: Yes — Parquet export includes sequence_id, event_timestamp, ingestion_timestamp and the same canonical ids; we include a schema file in /indices/schema.parquet.json describing types.

- S3 presigned PUT permissions: we provide a sample bucket policy and an IAM role example in the s3-delivery-instructions.pdf attachment. In short: allow s3:PutObject for prefix arn:aws:s3:::<your-bucket>/redwood-exports/<tenant-id> and s3:PutObjectAcl if you require ACLs; we recommend restricting by condition aws:SourceIp or aws:PrincipalArn when possible.

- Cost example: for planning, a 30-day mid-size tenant export (1–3GB compressed NDJSON + metadata) is typically priced at a one-time export fee in the $750–$1,500 range for Hosted. Dedicated customers are priced per-contract and exports are often included in an incident or compliance SLA. We’ll surface a formal quote in the SOW.

We’ll confirm Tue 6/1 10am PT and send a calendar invite; laura will cover transfer ops and david will cover retention/policy controls.

— Jonas

Onward, and attaching the referenced artifacts for your team to drop into the RFP.

[Attachments: redwood_audit_evidence_sample_manifest.json (example), export-schema-v2.md (schema), s3-delivery-instructions.pdf (transfer checklist)]
